item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 191146
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 AM PDT Mon Oct 19 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Trudy, located a couple of hundred miles offshore of
west-central Mexico.

South of Southern Mexico:
Showers and thunderstorms, associated with a trough of low pressure
located several hundred miles south of Guatemala, remain
disorganized. Environmental conditions appear conducive for
development, and a tropical depression is expected to form around
the middle of this week as the system moves westward to
west-northwestward at around 10 mph, well to the south of the coast
of southern Mexico.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...medium...50 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

$$
Forecaster Adams

item.title: Tropical Storm Trudy Public Advisory Number 25
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM MST Mon Oct 19 2026 
983 
WTPZ31 KNHC 191455
TCPEP1
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Trudy Advisory Number  25
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP212026
800 AM MST Mon Oct 19 2026
 
...TRUDY HOLDING STEADY OFF THE COAST OF WEST-CENTRAL MEXICO...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 800 AM MST...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...19.5N 108.5W
ABOUT 190 MI...310 KM WSW OF CABO CORRIENTES MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...60 MPH...95 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WSW OR 250 DEGREES AT 7 MPH...11 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...999 MB...29.50 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 AM MST (1500 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Trudy was 
located near latitude 19.5 North, longitude 108.5 West. Trudy is 
moving toward the west-southwest near 7 mph (11 km/h). A westward to 
west-southwestward motion is expected through tonight, followed by a 
gradual turn toward the northwest on Tuesday.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 60 mph (95 km/h) with higher gusts.
Weakening is expected over the next couple of days, and Trudy is
forecast to degenerate to a post-tropical cyclone by early Tuesday.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 70 miles (110 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 999 mb (29.50 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Trudy will continue affecting portions of
the coast of southwestern and west-central Mexico today. These
swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip current
conditions. Please consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 200 PM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Adams

item.title: Tropical Storm Trudy Forecast Discussion Number 25
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM MST Mon Oct 19 2026 
567 
WTPZ41 KNHC 191456
TCDEP1
 
Tropical Storm Trudy Discussion Number  25
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP212026
800 AM MST Mon Oct 19 2026
 
Convection has reignited near Trudy this morning, with very cold
cloud tops below -80C evident north and east of the estimated center
on infrared satellite imagery. However, an earlier GPM microwave
pass indicated that westerly wind shear is affecting the tropical
storm, with shear estimated at around 15 kt based on GFS and ECMWF
SHIPS guidance. Recent objective Dvorak intensity estimates from
UW-CIMSS range from 42-55 kt. Given the renewed convective activity
and the relatively consistent intensity estimates, the initial
intensity is maintained at 50 kt for this advisory.
 
Trudy is moving westward around 5 kt, steered by a low- to mid-level
ridge centered to its north. A westward to west-southwestward
motion, accompanied by a slower forward speed, is expected  through
tonight. A gradual turn toward the northwest is forecast on Tuesday
as a strong deep-layer trough advances southeastward over the
eastern Pacific toward the West Coast of the United States. The
latest NHC forecast track has been nudged slightly to the left of
the previous forecast, toward the HCCA and Google DeepMind
solutions.
 
Despite the recent uptick in convection, cooler sea surface
temperatures, increasingly dry mid-level air and an unfavorable
upper-level wind environment are expected to support weakening over
the next couple of days. ECMWF simulated satellite imagery suggests
that Trudy may struggle to maintain organized convection on Tuesday,
and the latest forecast calls for the system to become post-tropical
within 24 h. The latest NHC forecast is similar to the previous
forecast, lying near the upper end of the intensity guidance through
12 h and near the middle of the guidance thereafter. Trudy is
forecast to dissipate by 72 h.
 
Large swells will continue to affect the coast of southwestern
Mexico and west-central Mexico today, causing life-threatening surf
and rip current conditions at the beaches.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  19/1500Z 19.5N 108.5W   50 KT  60 MPH
 12H  20/0000Z 19.5N 108.7W   40 KT  45 MPH
 24H  20/1200Z 19.5N 109.4W   35 KT  40 MPH...POST-TROPICAL
 36H  21/0000Z 19.9N 110.0W   30 KT  35 MPH...POST-TROP/REMNT LOW
 48H  21/1200Z 20.3N 110.5W   25 KT  30 MPH...POST-TROP/REMNT LOW
 60H  22/0000Z 20.9N 111.0W   20 KT  25 MPH...POST-TROP/REMNT LOW
 72H  22/1200Z...DISSIPATED
 
$$
Forecaster Adams
